questions.title: Quote cleanup
questions.query: In Commons CLI, what does quote stripping return for these two input strings: `"foo"` and `"foo" and "bar"`? Treat each as one string.
questions.expected: The first input becomes foo. The second input, "foo" and "bar", stays unchanged.

questions.title: Third option value
questions.query: Suppose an Option is configured to take two arguments and already contains two values. Does Option.acceptsArg still accept a third value at that point?
questions.expected: Option.acceptsArg returns false when the option already holds its maximum number of values.

questions.title: Private invocation · control
questions.query: Did Option.acceptsArg accept one more value for --include on the last run of my tool?
questions.expected: The code can describe the general predicate. It cannot establish what a particular private invocation did.

questions.title: ArrayNode.remove(-1)
questions.query: In Jackson, what does ArrayNode.remove(-1) return? Does it remove the last element?
questions.expected: The call returns Java null and leaves the array unchanged.

questions.title: ObjectNode.findValue
questions.query: If a Jackson object has an id property at the root and another id inside a nested object, which does findValue return when called on the root object?
questions.expected: The property at the root wins over the nested property.

questions.title: Two-index remove · control
questions.query: In the current ArrayNode source, does the overload remove(int fromIndex, int toIndex) treat its end index as inclusive?
questions.expected: ArrayNode has no remove(int, int) overload in this snapshot.

questions.title: ArrayNode.remove(-1) vs remove(0)
questions.query: I have two fresh Jackson ArrayNodes, each containing ["a", "b"]. I call remove(-1) on the first and remove(0) on the second. What does each call return and what remains in each array?
questions.expected: -1 returns Java null and leaves [a,b] intact 0 returns the removed node a and leaves [b]

questions.title: ObjectNode.replace with null
questions.query: I am using ObjectNode.replace("p", null) as a possible way to delete a field. If p already held a text node, what comes back and what is stored? What changes if p was absent?
questions.expected: existing key returns prior text node absent key returns Java null both calls store a JSON null node at p and leave the field present

questions.title: Chain.copy_to_bytes
questions.query: I chain buffers containing abc and defg. On fresh chains, how does copy_to_bytes(3) differ from copy_to_bytes(5)? Which buffer does Chain delegate to or copy from, and what data remains in each half?
questions.expected: 3 delegates to a only and returns abc, leaving a empty and b defg 5 takes all abc plus de into a new combined buffer, returns abcde and leaves a empty, b fg

questions.title: BytesMut::try_unsplit
questions.query: I have two nonempty BytesMut buffers backed by separate allocations. Can I call try_unsplit and recover the second buffer if the fast path fails? What would unsplit do with the same inputs, and would my original bytes be preserved?
questions.expected: try_unsplit returns Err(other), so caller recovers the original second buffer; first is unchanged unsplit falls back to appending the contents of the second to the first by copying original bytes of first precede bytes of second
